done.why: I ran out of turns while sitting in the living room waiting for a serious wound from the thief to heal, so I could go back and finish him off for his bag and the egg I'd handed him.

about: It's a cut-down Zork. You loot a white house's underground empire for treasures and bring them back to the trophy case. In this version the far reaches are sealed off. The dam is "closed for inspection," the river has no boat, the reservoir passages run into still black water, the canyon view is roped off and the way down to the land of the dead is only a cold draught. What's left is the house, the troll, the maze, the Cyclops and a thief who guards his lair and makes you pay for every swing.

moments.note: Killed the troll in two blows and got 35 points right away.
The east exit from Damp Cave ends on a ledge over the river with no boat. It was the first sign that whole areas were sealed off.
The dam's 'CLOSED FOR INSPECTION -- The Management' sign is a funny, in-world way to close an area.
'Your load is too heavy, the sword not least of it.' I couldn't take the torch, so I had to drop things and go back up.
Praying at the altar took me straight out to the forest, a quick way back to the surface.
The chimney limit is spelled out exactly: you, your lamp and one thing more.
Saying 'odysseus' scared the Cyclops off, and he knocked a shortcut through to the living room.
The thief cut my throat the first time I swung at him. My belongings were scattered all over and I never found the sword again.
The thief backed off after one parry and left the chalice behind. That was an easy 15 points.
The altar hole is closed off with a nice description of sighing far below. Without Hades the bell, book and candles had no use.
I gave the thief the egg, hoping he'd open it, and then he kept fading into the gloom with it. Once I was told he 'left disgusted' while he was still described as standing in the room.
Two thief hits put me at 'serious wound, expect death soon', and over a dozen turns of waiting didn't heal it before the session ended.

wished: To find where my sword and skeleton key ended up after I died. 'Scattered about the Empire' gave me nothing to search on.
To unlock the grating in the clearing. My key went missing when I died.
To get the egg opened or get the canary back from the thief.
A faster way to heal than standing around waiting.
For the sealed areas (dam, river, Hades) to have something in them for the bell, book and candles.

lines.line: A board is nailed across it: "FLOOD CONTROL DAM #3. CLOSED FOR INSPECTION. -- The Management." You leave the dam to its inspection.
lines.why: A wry way of telling me where the edges of this world were.

lines.line: Somebody has sorted the near end of the rubble into neat heaps by size, smallest nearest.
lines.why: A strange, specific detail that made me think somebody lives down here. Probably the thief.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, your lamp and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: It states the rule plainly instead of just refusing.

lines.line: Your belongings, such as they were, have not come with you. They are scattered about the Empire, though somebody tidy has put the lamp back in the living room.
lines.why: A charming death message, but it cost me the sword and key for the rest of the game.

lines.line: You decide that whatever is down there has waited this long and can wait a little longer.
lines.why: The nicest of the closed-door messages. It made Hades feel real even though I couldn't go there.

fun.why: Early on it was satisfying: the troll, the torch, the Cyclops trick and the chalice. Then the thief fights turned into a slog of retreating, coming back up the stairs and waiting to heal.

engagement.why: Watching the score climb (35, 75, 85, 125, 140) kept me focused on the trophy case the whole time.

difficulty.why: Most puzzles were fair. The thief is the real wall: he killed me once and nearly did again, and healing is slow.

interestingness.why: The sealed-off edges are cleverly written and make the place feel bigger than it is. But with them shut, there were fewer things to pursue than I expected.

prose.why: The new text fits the classic voice well: dry, specific and often funny.
